Title: Diagnosis of test `testNodeSetOperations`

Details:
1. The test `testNodeSetOperations` fails on the assertion checking the XPath expression `$array > 0`.
2. The assertion uses the helper method `assertXPathValue` defined in `JXPathTestCase`. This method calls `ctx.getValue(xpath, resultType)`, setting lenient mode to false and comparing the expected and actual results.
3. The call `ctx.getValue(xpath, resultType)` delegates to `JXPathContextReferenceImpl.getValue(String, Class)`.
4. In `JXPathContextReferenceImpl.getValue(String, Class)`, the XPath expression is first compiled into an `Expression` object, then a more specific `getValue` method that accepts the compiled expression and result type is called.
5. Inside `JXPathContextReferenceImpl.getValue(String, Expression, Class)`, the value is first obtained by evaluating the expression without type conversion. Then, if the value is not null and a required result type is specified, a type check and possible conversion is performed.
6. If the value type cannot be converted to the requested result type, a `JXPathTypeConversionException` is thrown.
   
The failure in `testNodeSetOperations` likely arises from a type conversion issue or improper evaluation of the expression `$array > 0` when `$array` is a node set. The core problem could be with how node set operations are evaluated or how types are converted in `getValue`.

The diagnostic path points to issues possibly in the evaluation of the XPath expression, the type conversion logic, or the node set handling when greater-than operator is applied.

The best candidates for the fix are the evaluation and type conversion methods in the `JXPathContextReferenceImpl` class or related classes handling node set operations.

Suggested locations to fix:

org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.JXPathContextReferenceImpl.getValue(java.lang.String, java.lang.Class)  
org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.JXPathContextReferenceImpl.getValue(java.lang.String, org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.Expression, java.lang.Class)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
